title: Creating and Using Views
learning_outcomes: Describe the main purpose and behavior of creating and using views.
Apply a small SQLite example involving create view and verify the result.
Identify one failure mode, compatibility constraint, or data-integrity concern related to this topic.

content.intro: This lesson covers creating and using views as part of SQLite’s embedded relational database model. Work through one small example, verify the output, and then connect the result to the listed subtopics from the supplied curriculum.
content.why_it_matters: One-to-many joins can multiply rows and inflate aggregates if the reporting grain is not controlled.
content.task: Create a second example for creating and using views. Use at least one of these subtopics: CREATE VIEW, Views as reusable queries, Joining data through views. Predict the result, run it in a local SQLite environment or supported language binding, and document one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Include a minimal reproducible SQL statement or application snippet.
State the expected result before execution and compare it to the observed result.
Document one boundary/error case and the SQLite runtime assumptions.
hints: Start from the smallest subtopic and a fixture with only a few known rows.
Write the expected output before running the example; then change one input or predicate and compare.
If a feature fails, verify the linked SQLite version/build and isolate the failing statement before changing the schema.

common_mistakes.why: SQLite has specific type-affinity, NULL, configuration and version behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Check SQLite’s official documentation and the actual linked runtime; reduce to a small fixture.

common_mistakes.why: A query can run successfully while returning incorrect rows or an inflated aggregate.
common_mistakes.fix: Compare output to a hand-calculated expected result and test an edge case.

common_mistakes.why: Destructive SQL and migration experiments can permanently change a database.
common_mistakes.fix: Use a disposable file or in-memory database and verify backups before destructive operations.

content.run_instructions: Save the SQL to `lesson.sql`; run `sqlite3 -batch practice.db < lesson.sql`. For simple tabular output, add `.headers off` and `.mode list` in the shell or compare the returned rows in your API. Work only in a disposable practice database. CodeLeaf’s browser preview does not execute SQL.
content.troubleshooting: Check that the intended database file is open, statement terminators are present, the SQLite version supports the feature, and foreign-key settings are applied on the same connection. Run one statement at a time to isolate errors.
content.reset_steps: Close the shell and delete only the disposable `practice.db` file, or use a fresh `:memory:` connection. Never reset a production database.

items.title: CREATE VIEW
items.text: A view stores a named SELECT definition, not a separate copy of its result rows. Use it to centralize a stable query contract, and check which updates are permitted through the view.

items.title: Views as reusable queries
items.text: A view stores a named SELECT definition, not a separate copy of its result rows. Use it to centralize a stable query contract, and check which updates are permitted through the view.

items.title: Joining data through views
items.text: Write an explicit JOIN condition and know the relationship cardinality. A one-to-many join repeats parent rows; aggregate at the intended grain. For LEFT JOINs, a right-table filter in WHERE can remove unmatched left rows.

items.title: Assuming generic SQL behavior
items.text: Check SQLite’s own documentation and the actual linked runtime; standards-compliant engines can still differ in type handling, SQL extensions, and configuration.

items.title: Skipping verification
items.text: Reduce the example to the smallest fixture, inspect the schema and result rows, and repeat after changing one thing at a time.

items.title: Testing on valuable data
items.text: Use a disposable file or an in-memory database and a verified backup before destructive operations.

content_blocks.text: Recap. State the intended relationship in an explicit JOIN condition and check the result cardinality. Keep the creating and using views behavior explicit in code and document assumptions that a future maintainer would otherwise have to guess.

accessibility_notes: Use text labels and expected-output text rather than relying on diagram colors alone. SQL output is provided as text; enlarge type or use a screen reader as needed.
version_notes: SQLite feature availability varies with the library version and compile-time options. Verify SELECT sqlite_version() and the application binding before relying on newer features.
